item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
For what specific reason was the person who tried the Mario song punished? Did they try a test without following procedure? Is the Site Director upset about the containment breach caused by the song? How could the person who tried the song know what the effects would be?
Bearing in mind the previous entry discusses the total destruction of an entire site due to multiple severe containment breaches and the detonation of an on-site warhead, yet the Site Director did not immediately ban all testing based on that event, it seems off that the next test would lead to punishment when it was a comparatively lesser situation.

My point being, maybe it would fit better somewhere else other than immediately after 31. And if not, at minimum some justification for punishment would be nice.

This is great, but one little nitpick:

D-29234 is found at the same underpass with his head in his hands, weeping openly and muttering "she looked just like her". … D-29234 had a prior conviction for the murder of an ex-girlfriend, who was similar in appearance to the woman depicted in the SCP-3636-1 event.

How did D-29234 remember? Aren't all D-class given amnestics?

Still upvoted, though.
